review_text: I had this product years ago for hair removal. Then I bought a Remington laser so didn’t use this anymore. Lost it all in Harvey flood last summer. So I have sebaciois hyperplasia spots on my face. I was watching a YouTube video the other day, showing a doctor treating these spots with a needle laser type thing. I instantly remembered this tiny machine that had a needle for removing hairs. I wondered “hmm... will this work like the docs machine?” So I ordered it, read the directions which include DAMPENING YOUR FINGERS to get complete the electrical circuit. It will buzz once the needle is in contact with skin. When placed into a sebaciois hyperplasia spot, on power 10, it bubbles up the spot contents, making it easy to remove! Just like the docs thousands of dollars machine did! I am super happy. Yes, it’s a bit painful. But worth it.

review_text: This product does work to permanently remove unwanted hair but you need to have excellent lighting, a steady hand and patience. Also would advise getting extra styluses because they are very delicate and bend easily.

review_text: For the past 14 years I have sported either a full beard or a goatee. During that entire time, I have ALWAYS bought a NORELCO trimmer. Two months ago I replaced my old Norelco which lasted four years, and bouth this one. Although I do like the vacuum, the old models had a push out mini blade for the delicate work. This one doesn't. None of my older Norelco's ever slipped from their length setting. This one does, and when it does, it makes me look like I have mowed my face with a weedeater. Furthermore, the self adjusting comb never allows my mustache to come out right. There are always longer hairs towards the top of the mustache that I have to carefully try to cut by taking the brush off. In addition, I have followed the instructions very carefully and made sure not to over or undercharge the battery, but innevitably towards the end of my trim, the blades get a little sluggish. This is not a model to buy. Stay away from this model. Although I believe in Norelco, I will not buy one with this adjustable comb, and unfortunately it seems that they have put them on all their models. Until newer models come out that don't have them, I'll have to switch brands. Sorry Norelco!

review_text: I have been battling with coccyx pain for several months and needed a cushion that would support me while suspending my tailbone above the seat. This cushion was no help at all, because the foam was so squishy that it completely flattened out the instant I tried to sit on it. My tailbone was subjected to the same issues of compression and pain that I have with no cushion at all. In fact, it actually made the problem worse, because the foam in this cushion has so little substance that it crawled around underneath me and bunched up under my bottom, creating a large, uncomfortable lump right at the site of the pain! I desperately needed a cushion made of dense, firm, high quality foam, and this is simply not up to that standard. I returned it immediately. The fortunate thing is that the seller was easy to deal with, and was both cheerful and prompt with my refund. THEY EVEN REFUNDED MY RETURN SHIPPING! So, even though I cannot recommend this specific product, I would not hesitate to recommend the seller for anything else they are marketing on Amazon. I am sorry that I cannot give anyting better than one star to this cushion, but it really was worse than nothing for my particular problem. I am just glad that Amazon gives me the chance to review the seller's actions in a seperate forum. I was happy to give Cosmetic Solutions the highest rating possible!

review_text: The best investment I made in my dental care was deciding to purchase this Sonicare toothbrush. It's great for cleaning teeth--I mean my teeth really feel squeaky clean after using it. I do not feel that sticky film on the ridge of my teeth, as I do when using a regular toothrush. Another great feature of the toothbrush is that once powered up, it doesn't need to be recharged for well over a week (I'd think more closely to two weeks). I'm in a job where I'm doing more and more travel, so the convenient travel case that comes with it is heaven sent. Some of the other reviewers commented that the little pause/beep that the brush gives to indicate that it's time to move on to another quadrant in your mouth can be annoying. I agree; it is a little annoying. I tend to ignore that beep/pause, and continue in my normal brushing routine. To each his or her own. I've had my toothbrush now for almost 2 years, and I hope it will last for years to come. I recommended the toothbrush for my mom as well, and she loves it too. review_text: For two decades I have fought an uphill battle with a downhill class of products, and I'm throwing in the towel. I've abandoned this electric razor and gone back to a real razor (a basic Gillette Mach 3). I switched to a multi-headed electric razor over 20 years ago. "Stick with it for 30 days" the instructions implored. Yes, it got better, but never equalled my old 2-blade razor. The convenience suckered me in, and the habit was set. I meticulously cleaned and maintained my electric razors, but never attained a clean shave. But I stuck with it. Replaced the heads, and that worked for a while, but then same old same old. New electric razors seem to get worse. A little Phillips Philishave 30 worked pretty well (2 heads, *battery* powered), but not great. When this Arcitec came on board, I said "this is it!" Pricey, but there can be no better, right? Of all the electric razors I have used, I must say that this is the worst. The cleaning system works to a point, but there are inevitably hairs that get lodged in the razor head. And the razor head is effectively *NOT CLEANABLE* except by painstaking surgery to extract lodged hairs. And the shave? OK, this is not a scientific double-blinded study, but I do honestly believe that this razor provided me with the worst shave of all electric razors I have owned. It got me to jump ship and try a middle-of-the-road Gillette Mach 3. The result ... HEAVEN! Blades have gotten SO much better since 20 years ago. Super clean shave, no nics, no problems, no irritation ... why did I wait so long??
title: Fleeing back to a real razor

review_text: This product actually does whiten teeth. If it doesn't - you haven't been to a dentist in a while! You can't expect anything ( even dentist whitening) to whiten your teeth over night. A dentist whitening has you come back several times - depending on how white you want. Buy an extra soft toothbrush to use exclusively for the Magic Mud. This product WILL stain the bristles, so no use in using your expensive electric toothbrush. 3. Brush the product on your teeth in small, gentle, circular motions, focusing on the outsides of your teeth (the ones you want white). Spit SLOWLY with the water running, spitting as close as you can to the drain. Less mud will splash up your sink that way. 6. Swish water around in your mouth to get extra mud out from your gums and teeth. Slowly spit again. I then brush with my electric toothbrush with toothpaste as normal.

The lotion has a lot of really great things in it to do what it says (anti cellulite), you have retinol, eucalyptus, aloe, citrus, chamomile. Things like eucalyptus stimulates blood flow which could help reduce the look of cellulite however temporarily. Chamomile and aloe will help soothe the skin. All great things. Now the directions say massage the lotion in for several minutes. Again this is going to stimulate blood flow in the area and help REDUCE the look of cellulite. review_text: Purchased on a whim, to see if it would do what other products promised and didn't completely deliver. It does deliver. I have an old parquet floor that has aged and faded from before I bought my house. Other products advertised themselves as restorers for this kind of problem. They did after a fashion but still left the floor looking mostly the way it was before. Given my experience with the other products, I didn't have great hopes for this product, but to my surprise, just one application of this beeswax product has pretty much done the trick. The fading is pretty much gone and the wood has a warm, lustrous look now. It also brought back the original finish on some items of furniture I tried it on, simply wiping it on the wood. Instructions are minimal, so use caution with the sponge: it absorbs the wax, so there is a reserve of wax inside it. When I went to rinse off the dust from the sponge I squeezed it and wax came out with every squeeze. The sponge is large and the bottle is small, so getting the right amount of wax on the sponge takes some practice. Remember: a little goes a long way and the sponge absorbs the wax, so after a while use that instead of continuously reapplying new wax. A wonderful product.
title: Fortunate Discovery

review_text: “Skincare Travel Bag Included” uh…not really. The travel bag is huge and I definitely won’t use it as a travel bag. It’s 10x the size of the syringe cream. review_text: Like most reviewers, the prospect of 12 lip liners was too tempting to pass up. The good news is the manufacturer actually lists the ingredients on the box; I've taken a photo of the box so you can see the ingredients - personally, I don't recommend using products where you can't see the ingredients before you order. The pencils you get are an interesting range, and seem to vary from package to package. Mine were in a variety of colors; the one color I was looking for - a basic nude - was not in my package - but I got a range of plums (which I never wear) and pinks (which I rarely wear). If you've used any of your mom's pencils, you're familiar with carmine, which can flake. You have to be careful with the pressure used to avoid application debris, but it's the best to stop lipstick from bleeding or feathering. review_text: I was going to save this as a Christmas gift for my nieces but just could not resist and had to give it to them early. The foot spa uses batteries so I was able to do this anywhere and not have to worry about being close to an outlet. However, that could also be a "negative" as you have to worry about replacing batteries. We always have plenty of batteries at home anyway for our gadgets so it wasn't an issue. They had to "wait in line" for their turn while I painted their toes and gave them a stack of magazines to flip through. It was such a fun experience for them without having to spend a fortune, and in the safety of our home. The foot spa machine itself is pretty cool, and is almost like the one I have for myself. I did use warm water - the machine doesn't heat up or anything, so make sure you use lukewarm water for the little feets! I went a step further and even gave them an exfoliating foot scrub which is something I already have at home for myself. This is honestly the best $40 spent - an experience like this in a "real" salon and spa would have easily cost more than $40 for two girls. The great thing about this is that it is a suitable item for a wide range of ages, even after they've entered their teen years. I highly recommend this set.

review_text: First let me say: READ my review CAREFULLY to avoid an eyebrow malfunction like I experienced. Second, the tint works great!! Read on: I tinted my eyebrows thinking that it was OK to get some on the skin above and below my eyebrows and that it would wash off easily. After all, when I self-color my hair, the excess color wipes off my skin with no problem!! Ya, nope not true of this eyebrow tint. The excess wouldn’t come off!!! In hindsight, I had a very Low IQ moment. The instructions do tell you to test a patch of your skin before using it on your eyebrows. I didn’t do that. You should!! After I washed the tint off and attempted to wash the excess tint off, I saw a female Groucho Marx in the mirror. I tried removing the excess tint with 3 different face soaps, then regular body wash soap, then baking soda, then toothpaste. Tier 2: Shout with bleach, Comet spray w/bleach. Then Lysol wipes... moved onto nail polish remover. Then hairspray. But what actually did it was the 🚲 bike degreaser I use on my bike chain. Thank goodness because I was about ready to just dump an entire Costco-sized bottle of bleach on my face and let a higher power step in!! Worth noting: it was an eyebrow tint product from Slovenia so it probably doesn’t have the same ease of removal standards as American hair color products! Great product but just be very careful not to overdo it and don’t get it on the skin near your eyebrows!! Aim carefully at JUST your eyebrows!! PS. review_text: The wife and the MIL are huge fans of these face rollers, so we've tried just about every version and model out there. Although this does have a nice heavy, metal handle, the balls are PLASTIC. Stating in the title that it's a "Metal Facial Roller" is misleading because there are models where everything is indeed metal. In the description, it also says "our facial roller tool is High quality metal material". Ummmm... that's JUST THE HANDLE. The models we've tried with plastic balls had the fake metal paint water off, and some of them even crack after a while, so this is important in determining quality of the tool and the price that it should command. Most of the ones with plastic are priced around $8-10, while the all metal ones are $24-30. review_text: My girlfriend usually uses ColorEazy hair dye. This stuff is similar i how it works, but so much better. Like ColorEazy, you rub this into dry hair, wait twenty to twenty five minutes and rinse it out. This stuff, though, lathers up like a shampoo. What *I* really like about this (and she too) is that there is no chemical smell! I won't go as far as to say that it smells GOOD, but I will say that it doesn't smell bad. The coloring covered up all of her root with no trouble and seems to be holding up fine. The more you wash your hair, the less time the color will last, but you shouldn't be washing your hair every day, anyway. It strips all of the natural essential oils out that your hair needs. As with any new product you put on your body, you should test it on a small patch first - just to be sure that there will be no adverse reaction. The instructions tell you as much - as does every other hair dye out there. We did the test and there was no reaction whatsoever - no redness, no rash, no itching, no burning... either of her arm where we tested it or her scalp. For the price, and as little as it takes to get the job done, this is going to last practically forever. We can't recommend this enough!
